issues.description: The template expects students to implement the subroutine set_pixel at the marked TODO (label 'set_pixel:' in pixel.asm), and the problem text refers to a set_pixel routine called from main using the label set_pixel. The provided solution instead defines a label '.set_pixel' (leading dot/local-style label) in a different location and implements the pixel write there while main still calls 'set_pixel'. This creates a visibility/name mismatch: students following the template will implement/see a 'set_pixel' symbol, but the solution's implementation uses a different symbol naming/visibility ('.set_pixel') and placed the implementation at a different location than the template's TODO. This may lead to confusion or linker/assembler errors because the called symbol name and the defined symbol do not match or have different linkage/visibility.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure the subroutine symbol name and visibility match between template, problem description, and solution. Either: (a) define the function as 'set_pixel' (no leading dot) at the template's indicated TODO location so calls to 'set_pixel' resolve correctly, or (b) if using a local/leading-dot label, update the call sites to call the exact symbol used (and document the local/global naming). Prefer implementing 'set_pixel' exactly at the template's TODO to avoid student confusion about label naming and placement.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to the subroutine as set_pixel, but the solution defines the routine with a leading dot as .set_pixel. This inconsistent identifier naming for the same conceptual entity (the pixel-setting subroutine) can confuse students when mapping the exercise description to the provided code and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution's label from .set_pixel to set_pixel (or update the template/problem to consistently use .set_pixel) so the subroutine identifier matches exactly across problem statement, template and solution.
